A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same VisionZip work, with 28 readable pages and complete Appendices A–D. The text, equations, tables and visual material support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original image and video benchmark experiments, efficiency measurements, ablations and qualitative analyses in Sections 3–4 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experimental results, including the benchmark comparisons, efficiency measurements and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: Both versions use identical dominant-token selection, contextual-token merging and optional projector tuning. Section 2 and Algorithms 1–3, including the non-CLS adaptation in Appendix A.2, are unchanged.

E1.justification: The training datasets, image and video benchmarks, multi-turn dialogue example, longer-video example and COCO visualization scenarios are unchanged across the main text and appendices.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches: Tables 1 and 3 retain FastV and SparseVLM, while Table 2 retains SparseVLM. Vanilla baselines and appendix comparisons are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Both versions retain the same token budgets, model configurations, training fractions, evaluation metrics and benchmark averaging rules in Section 3 and Appendix B.

E4.justification: The feature-misalignment interventions in Table 5, dataset-compatibility ablation in Appendix B.1.6, supplementary efficiency analyses and attention visualizations in Appendix D are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both retain the same point-estimate reporting without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests. The appendix discussion of unstable small-benchmark results also matches.

E6.justification: Numerical entries and qualitative findings match throughout. Both report VisionZip's 94.0% normalized average with 64 tokens in Table 1 and 93.2% video average in Table 3; appendix results are likewise unchanged.

T1.justification: The FLOP expression, attention definitions in Equations 1 and 3, softmax derivative in Equation 2 and accompanying mathematical reasoning are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about visual-token redundancy, efficiency, preserved performance and applicability to image understanding, video understanding and multi-turn dialogue.

C2.justification: The explanations of information concentration, feature misalignment and projector adaptation remain identical. Applicability statements and qualifications concerning unstable benchmark results are also retained.

D1.justification: Hardware, learning rate, training fractions, token allocations and runtime disclosures are unchanged. The repository and demo access statements also match; the new author-contact footnote adds no technical implementation information.

R1.justification: Section 5, Appendix C and the 71-item reference list are unchanged. Positioning relative to earlier efficient VLM and KV-cache methods is retained.

P1.justification: V2 marks Zhuotao Tian as corresponding author and adds a contact footnote, while updating the arXiv version/date header. Scientific prose, terminology and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 2 moves from the left to the right column on page 2, with Algorithm 1 beneath it, and the opening pages reflow. Other differences are minute text-spacing adjustments; figure content, captions and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 adds corresponding-author identification and slightly rearranges the opening pages while retaining all scientific content and appendix evidence. These administrative and layout edits produce no meaningful net change in clarity, scientific support or reproducibility.
